title: Big Data for the Energy Transition: AI Governance and Personal Data Protection in Smart Energy Services
content: A household needs electricity, but this does not justify unrestricted analysis of its residents’ lives. Smart energy services blur this boundary when consumption records support billing, network operation, personalised advice and predictions about household behaviour. This article examines how these uses can be separated without obstructing useful innovation. A targeted synthesis of technical research and regulatory materials is combined with doctrinal analysis of European Union rules and five hypothetical service transitions. The resulting governance model links each processing operation to a defined service, a justified information need, a responsible actor and the consequences of ending that use. Its central finding is that access permission, a lawful processing basis and the justification for producing and using household inferences are distinct questions. Ending optional analytics therefore requires separating future analysis, the selected additional service, necessary settlement records and continuing electricity supply. The model distinguishes earned flexibility remuneration from future payments and from adverse consequences attached to refusing unrelated commercial uses. These are documentary and analytical findings, not measured energy savings or observations of providers. By connecting data exchange with service continuity, meaningful choice and reviewable decisions, the article addresses institutional conditions of the energy transition and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
